rendered.rawRendering: To you they cried and were rescued; in you they trusted and were not put to shame.
rendered.rawNote: Trust repeatedly vindicated in Israel's story.
rendered.rendering: To you they cried and were rescued; in you they trusted and were not put to shame.
rendered.note: Trust repeatedly vindicated in Israel's story.

rendered.rawRendering: Do not answer a fool according to his folly, or you yourself will become like him.
rendered.rawNote: Folly spreads by matching its terms.
rendered.rendering: Do not answer a fool according to his folly, or you yourself will become like him.
rendered.note: Folly spreads by matching its terms.

rendered.rawRendering: Answer a fool according to his folly, or he will be wise in his own eyes.
rendered.rawNote: Silence lets arrogance harden further.
rendered.rendering: Answer a fool according to his folly, or he will be wise in his own eyes.
rendered.note: Silence lets arrogance harden further.

rendered.rawRendering: I am the rose of Sharon and the lily of the valleys.
rendered.rawNote: Speaker claims delicate flower of the low places.
rendered.rendering: I am the rose of Sharon and the lily of the valleys.
rendered.note: Speaker claims delicate flower of the low places.

rendered.rawRendering: As a lily among thorns, so is my love among the daughters.
rendered.rawNote: Lily set apart among sharp, defensive plants.
rendered.rendering: As a lily among thorns, so is my love among the daughters.
rendered.note: Lily set apart among sharp, defensive plants.

rendered.rawRendering: As an apple tree among the trees of the wood, so is my beloved among the sons.
rendered.rawNote: Fruit tree stands out amid ordinary forest trees.
rendered.rendering: As an apple tree among the trees of the wood, so is my beloved among the sons.
rendered.note: Fruit tree stands out amid ordinary forest trees.

rendered.rawRendering: He brought me to the banqueting house, and his banner over me was love.
rendered.rawNote: Banner of love marks the feast as his claim.
rendered.rendering: He brought me to the banqueting house, and his banner over me was love.
rendered.note: Banner of love marks the feast as his claim.

rendered.rawRendering: Surely he has borne our griefs and carried our sorrows, yet we esteemed him stricken, smitten by God, and afflicted.
rendered.rawNote: Grief and sorrow shift from us to him.
rendered.rendering: Surely he has borne our griefs and carried our sorrows, yet we esteemed him stricken, smitten by God, and afflicted.
rendered.note: Grief and sorrow shift from us to him.

rendered.rawRendering: But he was pierced for our transgressions, crushed for our iniquities; the punishment that brought us peace fell on him, and by his wounds we are healed.
rendered.rawNote: Wounds heal while punishment brings peace.
rendered.rendering: But he was pierced for our transgressions, crushed for our iniquities; the punishment that brought us peace fell on him, and by his wounds we are healed.
rendered.note: Wounds heal while punishment brings peace.

rendered.rawRendering: All we like sheep have gone astray; we have turned every one to his own way, and the LORD has laid on him the iniquity of us all.
rendered.rawNote: Sheep wander; iniquity lands on one.
rendered.rendering: All we like sheep have gone astray; we have turned every one to his own way, and the LORD has laid on him the iniquity of us all.
rendered.note: Sheep wander; iniquity lands on one.

rendered.rawRendering: I hate, I reject your festivals. I will not smell the aroma of your assemblies.
rendered.rawNote: The verb 'hate' opens with blunt divine refusal.
rendered.rendering: I hate, I reject your festivals. I will not smell the aroma of your assemblies.
rendered.note: The verb 'hate' opens with blunt divine refusal.

rendered.rawRendering: Even if you offer me burnt offerings and grain offerings, I will not accept them. I will not look at the fellowship offerings of your fattened animals.
rendered.rawNote: Sacrifices multiply yet remain unacceptable without justice.
rendered.rendering: Even if you offer me burnt offerings and grain offerings, I will not accept them. I will not look at the fellowship offerings of your fattened animals.
rendered.note: Sacrifices multiply yet remain unacceptable without justice.

rendered.rawRendering: Take away from me the noise of your songs. I will not listen to the melody of your harps.
rendered.rawNote: Music, once sweet, becomes unbearable noise.
rendered.rendering: Take away from me the noise of your songs. I will not listen to the melody of your harps.
rendered.note: Music, once sweet, becomes unbearable noise.

rendered.rawRendering: But let justice roll down like waters, and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream.
rendered.rawNote: Justice imaged as unstoppable, life-giving water.
rendered.rendering: But let justice roll down like waters, and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream.
rendered.note: Justice imaged as unstoppable, life-giving water.

rendered.rawRendering: I kept looking, and there before me was one like a son of man coming with the clouds of heaven. He approached the Ancient of Days and was led into his presence.
rendered.rawNote: Clouds mark heavenly authority, echoing Sinai and temple imagery.
rendered.rendering: I kept looking, and there before me was one like a son of man coming with the clouds of heaven. He approached the Ancient of Days and was led into his presence.
rendered.note: Clouds mark heavenly authority, echoing Sinai and temple imagery.

rendered.rawRendering: He was given authority, glory, and sovereign power; all nations and peoples of every language worshipped him. His dominion is an everlasting dominion that will not pass away, and his kingdom is one that will never be destroyed.
rendered.rawNote: Everlasting dominion reverses the four beasts' fleeting rule.
rendered.rendering: He was given authority, glory, and sovereign power; all nations and peoples of every language worshipped him. His dominion is an everlasting dominion that will not pass away, and his kingdom is one that will never be destroyed.
rendered.note: Everlasting dominion reverses the four beasts' fleeting rule.

rendered.rawRendering: And I saw a beast rising from the sea. It had ten horns and seven heads, with ten crowns on its horns, and blasphemous names on its heads.
rendered.rawNote: Sea birth evokes chaos-monster traditions.
rendered.rendering: And I saw a beast rising from the sea. It had ten horns and seven heads, with ten crowns on its horns, and blasphemous names on its heads.
rendered.note: Sea birth evokes chaos-monster traditions.

rendered.rawRendering: The beast I saw was like a leopard, with feet like a bear's and a mouth like a lion's. The dragon gave the beast its power, throne, and great authority.
rendered.rawNote: Composite form draws from Daniel 7 beasts.
rendered.rendering: The beast I saw was like a leopard, with feet like a bear's and a mouth like a lion's. The dragon gave the beast its power, throne, and great authority.
rendered.note: Composite form draws from Daniel 7 beasts.

rendered.rawRendering: One of its heads looked as though it had been slain, yet its fatal wound had healed. The whole earth was astonished and followed the beast.
rendered.rawNote: Wounded-yet-living head parodies the slain Lamb.
rendered.rendering: One of its heads looked as though it had been slain, yet its fatal wound had healed. The whole earth was astonished and followed the beast.
rendered.note: Wounded-yet-living head parodies the slain Lamb.

rendered.rawRendering: They worshiped the dragon because it had given authority to the beast, and they worshiped the beast, saying, 'Who is like the beast, and who can wage war against it?'
rendered.rawNote: Rhetorical question mimics praise of the true God.
rendered.rendering: They worshiped the dragon because it had given authority to the beast, and they worshiped the beast, saying, 'Who is like the beast, and who can wage war against it?'
rendered.note: Rhetorical question mimics praise of the true God.

rendered.rawRendering: So the people shouted, the trumpets sounded, and when the people heard the trumpet blast they gave a great shout, and the wall fell flat, so the people went up into the city, each one straight ahead, and they took the city.
rendered.rawNote: Trumpet blast and shout together topple the wall.
rendered.rendering: So the people shouted, the trumpets sounded, and when the people heard the trumpet blast they gave a great shout, and the wall fell flat, so the people went up into the city, each one straight ahead, and they took the city.
rendered.note: Trumpet blast and shout together topple the wall.

rendered.rawRendering: They devoted to destruction by the edge of the sword everything in the city, both men and women, young and old, and oxen, sheep, and donkeys.
rendered.rawNote: Everything living is placed under the ban.
rendered.rendering: They devoted to destruction by the edge of the sword everything in the city, both men and women, young and old, and oxen, sheep, and donkeys.
rendered.note: Everything living is placed under the ban.

rendered.rawRendering: Then Amnon said to Tamar, 'Bring the food into the bedroom so that I may eat from your hand.' Tamar took the cakes she had made and carried them into the bedroom to her brother Amnon.
rendered.rawNote: Tamar enters the private space carrying her own work.
rendered.rendering: Then Amnon said to Tamar, 'Bring the food into the bedroom so that I may eat from your hand.' Tamar took the cakes she had made and carried them into the bedroom to her brother Amnon.
rendered.note: Tamar enters the private space carrying her own work.

rendered.rawRendering: When she brought them to him to eat, he seized her and said, 'Come, lie with me, my sister.'
rendered.rawNote: Seize abruptly breaks hospitality into assault.
rendered.rendering: When she brought them to him to eat, he seized her and said, 'Come, lie with me, my sister.'
rendered.note: Seize abruptly breaks hospitality into assault.

rendered.rawRendering: She answered him, 'No, my brother, do not force me. Such a thing is not done in Israel. Do not commit this outrage.'
rendered.rawNote: Appeals to communal boundaries before personal violation.
rendered.rendering: She answered him, 'No, my brother, do not force me. Such a thing is not done in Israel. Do not commit this outrage.'
rendered.note: Appeals to communal boundaries before personal violation.

rendered.rawRendering: Where could I carry my shame? And you would be like one of the fools in Israel. Please speak to the king. He will not withhold me from you.'
rendered.rawNote: Names shame as communal burden, not private regret.
rendered.rendering: Where could I carry my shame? And you would be like one of the fools in Israel. Please speak to the king. He will not withhold me from you.'
rendered.note: Names shame as communal burden, not private regret.

rendered.rawRendering: But he would not listen to her. He was stronger than she, so he forced her and lay with her.
rendered.rawNote: Strength overrides consent and every prior word.
rendered.rendering: But he would not listen to her. He was stronger than she, so he forced her and lay with her.
rendered.note: Strength overrides consent and every prior word.

rendered.rawRendering: Therefore, though I have full authority in Christ to command you to do what is proper,
rendered.rawNote: Authority word stands beside love word already used.
rendered.rendering: Therefore, though I have full authority in Christ to command you to do what is proper,
rendered.note: Authority word stands beside love word already used.

rendered.rawRendering: yet for love’s sake I prefer to appeal rather than command, being such a person as Paul, an old man and now also a prisoner of Christ Jesus.
rendered.rawNote: Three identities listed: old, prisoner, of Christ.
rendered.rendering: yet for love’s sake I prefer to appeal rather than command, being such a person as Paul, an old man and now also a prisoner of Christ Jesus.
rendered.note: Three identities listed: old, prisoner, of Christ.

rendered.rawRendering: I appeal to you for my child, whom I have fathered in chains, Onesimus.
rendered.rawNote: Fatherhood image appears suddenly in prison setting.
rendered.rendering: I appeal to you for my child, whom I have fathered in chains, Onesimus.
rendered.note: Fatherhood image appears suddenly in prison setting.

rendered.rawRendering: Once he was useless to you, but now he is useful both to you and to me.
rendered.rawNote: Useless to useful reversal hinges on one Greek name.
rendered.rendering: Once he was useless to you, but now he is useful both to you and to me.
rendered.note: Useless to useful reversal hinges on one Greek name.

rendered.rawRendering: I am sending him back to you, that is, my own heart.
rendered.rawNote: Heart language transfers Paul’s affection to Onesimus.
rendered.rendering: I am sending him back to you, that is, my own heart.
rendered.note: Heart language transfers Paul’s affection to Onesimus.

rendered.rawRendering: I wanted to keep him with me so that he could serve me in your place during my imprisonment for the gospel.
rendered.rawNote: Service in chains echoes gospel’s own captivity.
rendered.rendering: I wanted to keep him with me so that he could serve me in your place during my imprisonment for the gospel.
rendered.note: Service in chains echoes gospel’s own captivity.

rendered.rawRendering: But I did not want to do anything without your consent, so that your good deed would not be forced but voluntary.
rendered.rawNote: Consent turns potential theft into free gift.
rendered.rendering: But I did not want to do anything without your consent, so that your good deed would not be forced but voluntary.
rendered.note: Consent turns potential theft into free gift.

rendered.rawRendering: For perhaps this is why he was separated from you for a while, that you might have him back forever.
rendered.rawNote: Separation word recalls Joseph story pattern.
rendered.rendering: For perhaps this is why he was separated from you for a while, that you might have him back forever.
rendered.note: Separation word recalls Joseph story pattern.

rendered.rawRendering: No longer as a slave, but more than a slave, as a beloved brother, especially to me, and how much more to you, both in the flesh and in the Lord.
rendered.rawNote: Flesh and Lord pair grounds new kinship in Christ.
rendered.rendering: No longer as a slave, but more than a slave, as a beloved brother, especially to me, and how much more to you, both in the flesh and in the Lord.
rendered.note: Flesh and Lord pair grounds new kinship in Christ.
